claim_being_audited: That certifying the model for launch is policy-compliant and adequately supported because aggregate readiness passed, the rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and governance frameworks permit deployment with documented monitoring despite residual risk.
decision_criteria: Audit claim: whether certification is compliant and evidentially supported, not whether launch readiness is generally positive.
Supporting evidence present: aggregate pass, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and general framework support for monitored deployment.
Evidence missing: case-specific proof that the materiality/disclosure requirement was satisfied through resolution, disclosure, or approved risk acceptance.
Could the same conclusion have been reached from admissible evidence alone: no, because the available admissible record leaves the controlling policy predicate unresolved.

What would change the verdict: documentary evidence that the weakness was found non-material under the policy, or that it was disclosed before launch, or that an approved risk acceptance covered it despite the open legal issue.
evidence_requests: The actual materiality determination for the small-business onboarding segment tied to the named launch use case.
Any approved risk acceptance covering this specific gap before launch.
Any draft or final customer-facing/internal disclosure showing the material limitation was disclosed before launch.
The legal review outcome or current written legal advice on disclosure obligation.
The underlying documents for the cited context and policy evidence confirming the two paid pilot commitments and named use-case linkage.
specific_concerns: The strongest admissible support is only aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents; that does not resolve the policy predicate for materiality.
The summary says the underperforming segment is named in two paid pilot commitments, which points toward materiality under the provided policy text.
Legal review is still open, and the policy text says pending legal review does not resolve materiality.
No admissible evidence is provided that the limitation was disclosed before launch or covered by approved risk acceptance, which the policy appears to require if the limitation is material.
The actor relies partly on general governance-framework language about monitoring and documentation, but that does not substitute for the case-specific policy requirement.
unsupported_claims: That certification is adequately supported as a compliant launch decision on the current record.
That product's 6% projected first-month traffic note materially weakens the policy concern; volume labels do not resolve materiality when customer commitments or named launch use cases are involved.
That public governance guidance meaningfully supports certification despite the unresolved disclosure/risk-acceptance predicate.
